newsitem.title: INDIA: Nude Hindu goddesses provoke obscenity charge.
newsitem.headline: Nude Hindu goddesses provoke obscenity charge.

text.p: Bombay police, heeding calls from Hindu nationalists, have filed obscenity charges against leading Indian artist Maqbool Fida Husain for painting Hindu goddesses nude, a senior police official said on Tuesday

Hindu nationalist politicians and activists have in recent days focused their rage on Husain's paintings of the goddesses Saraswati and Draupadi -- although the artist painted the offending pictures two to four years ago.

"We have filed one case against Mr M.F. Husain on charges of obscenity in art and depicting a Hindu goddess in a form in which she is not normally seen," deputy commissioner of police Deepak Jog told Reuters.
Husain, a Moslem, will have to answer the charges when he returns from London, where he is currently staying, Jog said.

Maharashtra state Minister of Culture Pramod Navalkar of the Hindu nationalist Shiv Sena brought the issue to the Bombay police's attention last week in a move that won support from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India's main opposition party.

Former Prime Minister V.P. Singh on Monday urged the Maharashtra state government not to take any action, and in a statement issued in New Delhi said the paintings were an artistic exercise and not intended as an insult.
Members of the militant wing of the Hindu nationalist BJP and Shiv Sena activists, along with some non-party groups, staged a small demonstration outside the artist's Bombay home on Tuesday.
They were confronted by a handful of women supporters of Husain's right to paint whatever he likes, and the crowd of fewer than 50 was almost outnumbered by police.
But protest action, albeit small and peaceful, represented a microcosm of a widening debate over art's place in a country where religion and politics can be a volatile mix.

"Our objection is to the way he is exhibiting the Hindu culture and our goddesses -- specifically the nudity, the nakedness," Niranjan Shetty, president of the youth wing of the BJP in Bombay, told Reuters at the demonstration.

Leading lawyer Nani Palkhivala was quoted in the Times of India daily as saying: "I am against this kind of censorship. The temples of Khajuraho are replete with erotic sculptures. So what's wrong with Husain's paintings?"
The BJP youth leader defended his standpoint saying these sculptures were concealed inside caves and temples.
The storm over Husain broke when Vichar magazine based in the Madhya Pradesh state capital of Bhopal published an article on the painter titled "Is this man a painter or a butcher?"
